newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank cuts borrowing rate to 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank cuts borrowing rate to 10 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank on Friday said it cut its overnight borrowing rate to 10 percent from 10.25 percent.

This is the second time this week it has lowered the rate. Early this week, it dropped its overnight borrowing rate to 10.25 from 10.4375 percent following the sharp fall in Treasury bill rates on Monday.
The Central Bank left its overnight lending rate unchanged at 12.75 percent.
Its borrowing rates on the one- and two-month term reverse repos were likewise trimmed by 0.25 percentage points each to 10.0625 and 10.125 percent, respectively.
The Central Bank's move surprised the market because it came at the end of the week when there is normally no action, traders said.

But a foreign bank dealer said the current level of the overnight borrowing rate was what the market had expected after the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate plunged to 10.159 from 10.564 percent on Monday due to a dearth of investment instruments.
Banks had been staying away from the term reverse repos which have a 20 percent tax.
"It (the Central Bank) did not want to jolt the market," the dealer said, referring to the Central Bank's first rate cut early this week.
The Central Bank's move on Monday did not trigger peso speculation.
